chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: Great nights after no sleep: Ella's tour and the Hamburg encores
summary: Jones describes exhausted one-nighters with Ella Fitzgerald that produced great performances, including endless ovations in Hamburg.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And sometimes when there's been no
sleep and everybody's physically miserable, sometimes you get one of your greatest evenings^ of music.

Yes. Well, sometimes I've been -- I won't say I've been a victim, but I've shared those experiences. There are times when we would go, especially with Ella -- not so much with Sarah, because we didn't travel that hard with Sarah -- but with Ella, doing the one nighters the way we did it, I would say, "Boy --," talking to myself now, say, "Jones, I hope you can make it tonight." And it would be one of the best performances, and I don't even know what -- where the energy came from. And the chemistry worked. We had one experience in Hamburg, Germany, where we were just getting standing ovations, standing ovations, one after another. We went back and played the end of the concert, went back and changed our clothes, to go to the airport, and they wouldn't let us leave. They just came around and stood around the stage, you know?
Yeah. And the band had to come back too. So we came and played in our regular -- we were all dressed up in tuxedos.
We were so tired, but the people loved it, and you had to give it to them, you know.
You know, you've got to give it to them, because if they love you you'd better be sure -- call yourself lucky, you know, because they don't have to.
